the influence of the properties of the boiling fluid can be taken into account in a semiempirical correlation by the introduction of a property factor.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermodynamic properties have only a small impact on the heat transfer coefficient, but the thermophysical properties have a significant effect on the heat transfer.
the heat transfer performance is not only determined by the thermophysical properties, but also by the surface structure of the heating surface.
a correct description of this influence is essential for a successful prediction of the heat fluxes in the nucleate boiling regime.
